_exec_summary.SummaryText:
Baxter Healthcare of Puerto Rico, LLC (Baxter) manufactures inhaled anesthetics in its facility located at Route 3, Km. 144.2, in Guayama, Puerto Rico. Its NAICS code is 32541.

Baxter Guayama is committed to the protection of the environment, health and safety of our employees and neighbors. The EHS (Environmental, Health and Safety) Associate Director reports dotted line to the Plant Manager and ensures that jobs, tasks, projects, etc. to be performed are evaluated by the EHS department.

For the Process Safety Program and Risk Management Program, roles and responsibilities are defined to assure all changes and repairs are completed following Recognized and Generally Accepted Good Engineering Practices.

Baxter has policies and procedures that define administrative and engineering controls for the prevention of accidental releases and response to emergencies. Senior management roles and responsibilities are defined in job descriptions, policies, and procedures to ensure compliance with EHS regulations.

The Baxter Guayama Facility manufactures three types of anesthesia (Isoflurane, Desflurane, and Sevoflurane) in which the processes include at least one chemical (chlorine (Cl2) and/or hydrofluoric acid (HF)) that exceed 40 CFR Part 68 Risk Management Program (RMP) threshold limits. 

Chlorine and Hydrofluoric Acid are used in the manufacturing reaction processes as follows:

1)	Hydrofluoric Acid (HF), Anhydrous 100 % CAS No. 7664-39-3:

HF is present on site above RMP threshold limits in the Desflurane and Sevoflurane manufacturing processes. There is an HF storage tank that is capable of storing 53,301 lb (based on full capacity). From the storage tank, HF is transferred to the Sevoflurane and Desflurane manufacturing processes. Process tank emergency vents are connected to an emergency scrubber system.

The Desflurane Process has two fluorination reactors, although only one is used at a time in the reaction step, and the Sevoflurane Process has one Fluorin

ation reactor. A trailer mounted HF iso-container is included in the Sevoflurane process (41,477 lb) that remains on-site until final products from batches supplied by the HF in the iso-container pass QA inspection. Once QA inspection is passed, the iso-container is removed from the property. 

2)	Chlorine, CAS No. 7782-505:

Cl2 is handled as a liquefied gas in 2,000 lb (one-ton) pressurized cylinders. Cl2 cylinders are  managed at a storage rack where a maximum of 52,000 lb may be present, which exceeds the RMP threshold. Both the Isoflurane and Sevoflurane processes use Cl2 in chlorination reactions. Cl2 is supplied to each processes from its respective enclosed Chlorine Room where Cl2 cylinders are connected to the processes. The Chlorine Rooms are serviced by a scrubber system to prevent a gaseous release to atmosphere. 

The Baxter General Accident Release Prevention Program guides the sites compliance efforts for RMP, 29 CFR § 1910.119 Process Safety Management (PSM), and 6 CFR Part 27 Chemical Facility Anti-Terrorism Standards.

As the covered processes are subject to PSM requirements, all covered processes fall under the RMP Program 3 Prevention Program.

Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Material Batch Records (MBRs) describe specific steps necessary to safely operate the processes. SOPs include Process Safety information, consequences of deviations, and controls (administrative, engineering, and personal protective equipment) for safe operation and to minimize any impacts to processes, Baxter personnel, and the surrounding community in the event of an emergency. Training related to SOPs and MBRs is provided on a regular basis, when processes are impacted by changes, and after the occurrence of a Process Safety Incident. The training curriculum is formalized throughout the site and curricula are assigned to employees and contractors based on their roles and responsibilities.

The management of change (MOC) program includes evaluation for change

s related to the process. As part of MOC evaluations, a process hazard analysis (PHA) may be required before the change is executed. Pre-startup safety review are performed before operation of a new or modified process or facility.

PHAs are performed according to the RMP regulation or more often if a change impacts the safety of the process. During PHAs , risks and hazards are evaluated for each process component.

Baxter contractor roles and responsibilities are defined as part of the procedures, and contractor performance is evaluated each year. An annual meeting is coordinated with contractors to ensure they know Baxter safety rules. Each contractor must complete annual training provided by Baxter in which safety rules, roles, and responsibilities are reviewed, and contractors demonstrate that they understand the rules and their roles and responsibilities. As part of the pre-selection process, the contractor's safety program and training evidence is evaluated.

Baxters safety programs include procedures on lockout out/tag out, hot work permits, confined space entry, etc. that require the use of engineering and administrative controls to maintain process control during routine and non-routine activities.

Baxters mechanical integrity program includes preventive maintenance, calibration, and routine inspection of process critical equipment. Also, the operational status of safety system, including alarms and fire systems, is routinely inspected and tested as part of the program. Shutdowns are scheduled throughout the year. Mechanical integrity testing is conducted based on the requirements of applicable codes, standards, and regulations by specialized contractors and onsite personnel.

Compliance audits are conducted according to the RMP regulation.

Baxters incident investigation program requires incident reporting and investigation. Incidents related to environmental releases, safety, property damage, product loss, security, occupational health, and near mis

ses are investigated as part of the program. As part of the incident investigation, factors that contribute to the incidents are identified with defined corrective and preventive actions.

Baxter has had no releases in the past five years that require reporting per RMP reporting requirements.  

The emergency response program consists of the following elements: Organization and Procedure for Fire Control, Hurricane Emergency Plan, Emergency Evacuation Alarms, and Procedure for Area and Emergency Meeting Point Coordinators.

As part of the Baxter emergency system, employees from different shifts and areas are trained in emergency responses to fires, spills, and other emergencies such that the site fire brigade is fully staffed at all times. As part of the fire brigade training program, classroom training and drills are provided on topics including the use of chlorine release mitigation kits, Level A protective gear, self-contained breathing apparatus, hazardous materials response, fire extinguishers, fixed and portable firefighting equipment, and monitoring equipment for environmental and confined space monitoring.

Local agencies, including the municipal fire department are knowledgeable about the Baxter facility through  the SPCC and SWPP Plan, other EPA required reports, and participate in site tabletop and full emergency response exercises. Currently, the LEPC does not have periodic meeting, but Baxter personnel keep local agencies informed in the event an incident that may affect the surrounding community and participate in site tabletop and full emergency response exercises

For the next year, Baxter has planned a number of initiatives to maintain safety performance. For example, continuing the hazard identification (HAZID) reporting, monitoring, and recognition as well as near miss event reporting. In addition, the Baxter Start When Certain Program is an (EHS) program that gives employees and contractors the authority and responsibility to perform their work

safely and to stop work if an unsafe condition, behavior, or hazard is observed. The Start When Certain Program provides clear and simple guidance that outlines safe work practices, responsibilities, and controls for eight high-risk activities (confined space, driver safety, electrical safety, hot work, LOTO, machine guarding, powered industrial trucks, and working at heights).

When comparing this resubmission with the 2024 submittal for covered processes, no new storage tanks or areas were built.
